title: panic
concept: panic triggers an unrecoverable error — use it when continuing execution would be dangerous or impossible.
why: Some errors have no recovery path. Continuing after them would produce garbage results or corrupt data. panic stops the program immediately.
tips: Use panic only for truly unrecoverable errors — the caller has NO chance to handle it
Include enough context in the message to diagnose the issue without reproducing it
panic is always active (unlike assert) — safe for production safety checks
Consider whether the error could be handled with Result before reaching for panic
common_mistakes: Using panic for recoverable errors — file not found should be Result, not panic
Calling panic in library code that applications depend on — libraries should return errors
Writing generic panic messages like "error" or "failed" — be specific about what went wrong
